title.zh: 卷七十 唐書46: 列傳22 元行欽 夏魯奇 姚洪 李嚴 李仁矩 康思立 張敬達
title.en: Volume 70 Book of Later Tang 46: Biographies 22 - Yuan Xingqin, Xia Luqi, Yao Hong, Li Yan, Li Renju, Kang Sili, Zhang Jingda
title.raw: 卷七十 唐書46: 列傳22 元行欽 夏魯奇 姚洪 李嚴 李仁矩 康思立 張敬達 Volume 70 Book of Later Tang 46: Biographies 22 - Yuan Xingqin, Xia Luqi, Yao Hong, Li Yan, Li Renju, Kang Sili, Zhang Jingda

sentences.zh: 元行欽，本幽州劉守光之愛將。

translations.literal: Yuan Xingqin was originally a favored general of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xingqin had originally been a favorite general of Liu Shouguang of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 守光之奪父位也，令行欽攻大恩山，又令殺諸兄弟。

translations.literal: When Shouguang usurped his father's position, he ordered Xingqin to attack Da'en Mountain and also ordered him to kill all his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang seized power from his father, he sent Xingqin to attack Mount Da'en and had him put his brothers to death.

sentences.zh: 天祐九年，周德威攻圍山州，守光困蹙，令行欽於山北募兵，以應契丹。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei besieged Shan Prefecture; Shouguang was hard pressed and ordered Xingqin to recruit troops north of the mountains to coordinate with the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Tianyou, Zhou Dewei laid siege to Shan Prefecture. With Shouguang besieged and desperate, he ordered Xingqin to raise troops north of the mountains to join forces with the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 時明宗為將，攻行欽於山北，與之接戰，矢及明宗馬鞍，既而以勢迫來降。

translations.literal: At that time the Mingzong was a general; he attacked Xingqin north of the mountains and joined battle with him. An arrow struck the Mingzong's saddle; subsequently, pressed by circumstances, Xingqin came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The future Mingzong was then serving as a general. He attacked Xingqin in the northern hills and fought him in pitched battle—an arrow struck the Mingzong's saddle—until finally, overcome by the situation, Xingqin submitted.

sentences.zh: 明宗憐其有勇，奏隸為假子，後因從征討，恩禮特隆。

translations.literal: The Mingzong took pity on his bravery, memorialized to have him enrolled as an adoptive son, and afterward, because he followed on campaigns, bestowed exceptional favor and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingzong admired his valor and petitioned to take him as an adopted son. Thereafter, as Xingqin campaigned beside him, he received exceptional favor and respect.

sentences.zh: 常臨敵擒生，必有所獲，名聞軍中。

translations.literal: He often faced the enemy and took prisoners alive; he always gained something, and his fame spread through the army.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he habitually took living captives and never came away empty-handed; his reputation rang through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 莊宗東定趙、魏，選驍健置之麾下，因索行欽，莊宗不得已而遣之。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangzong secured Zhao and Wei in the east, he selected the brave and stalwart and placed them under his command; he therefore demanded Xingqin, and the Zhuangzong, having no choice, sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuangzong conquered Zhao and Wei in the east, he drafted the finest fighters into his personal following and specifically asked for Xingqin. The Zhuangzong had no choice but to release him.

sentences.zh: 時有散指揮都頭，名為散員，命行欽為都部署，賜姓，名紹榮。

translations.literal: At that time there was a scattered-command chief-of-staff post called "scattered member"; he appointed Xingqin as commander-in-chief of deployment, bestowed a surname, and named him Shaorong.
translations.idiomatic: There was then a corps of unattached commanders known as the "scattered members"; the Zhuangzong made Xingqin their chief deployer, granted him the imperial surname, and gave him the name Shaorong.

sentences.zh: 莊宗好戰，勇於大敵，或臨陣有急兵，行欽必橫身解鬥翼衛之。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong loved battle and was bold against great enemies; whenever on the battlefield there was pressing danger, Xingqin would always throw himself across the fight to shield and guard him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong was eager for combat and fearless before formidable foes. Whenever danger closed in on the field, Xingqin would throw himself into the fray to fight off attackers and shield him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗營於德勝也，與汴軍戰於潘張，王師不利，諸軍奔亂。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangzong encamped at Desheng, he fought the Bian armies at Panzhang; the royal army fared poorly and all forces fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: While the Zhuangzong was encamped at Desheng, his forces met the Bian army at Panzhang. The imperial troops were routed and the whole army broke in panic.

sentences.zh: 莊宗得三四騎而旋，中野為汴軍數百騎攢槊攻之，事將不測，行欽識其幟，急馳一騎，奮劍斷二矛，斬一級，汴軍乃解圍，翼莊宗還宮。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong got away with only three or four horsemen in his retreat; in the open fields several hundred Bian horsemen gathered their spears to attack him—the outcome was about to become desperate—when Xingqin recognized their banners, spurred a single horse forward in haste, brandished his sword and severed two spears and cut off one head; the Bian army then broke the encirclement, and he escorted the Zhuangzong back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong escaped with only three or four riders. In the open country several hundred Bian cavalry closed in with leveled spears, and the situation was on the verge of disaster. Xingqin recognized their banners, spurred forward alone, swung his sword to snap two spears and cut down one man, and the Bian troops broke the encirclement. He then escorted the Zhuangzong safely back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 莊宗因流涕言曰：「富貴與卿共之。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong thereupon said with tears streaming: "Wealth and honor I shall share with you.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong wept and said, "Whatever wealth and honor are mine, I will share them with you.

sentences.zh: 」自是寵冠諸將，官至檢校太傅、忻州刺史。

translations.literal: " From then on his favor surpassed all other generals; he reached the posts of honorary Grand Tutor and prefect of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " From that day his favor outstripped every other general's, and he rose to honorary Grand Tutor and prefect of Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗平梁，授武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangzong pacified the Liang, he was appointed military governor of the Wuning army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhuangzong conquered the Liang, he was made military governor of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 嘗因內宴群臣，使相預會，行欽官為保傅，當地褥下坐。

translations.literal: Once, at an inner banquet for the ministers with chief commissioners in attendance, Xingqin's office was that of guardian-tutor, and he was to sit on the floor below the mat.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the Zhuangzong held an inner banquet for his ministers, with chief commissioners present. Xingqin held the rank of guardian-tutor and was assigned a seat on the floor below the mat.

sentences.zh: 酒酣樂作，莊宗敘生平戰陣之事，因左右顧視，曰：「紹榮安在？

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep and music began, the Zhuangzong recounted battles of his life, then looked to left and right and said: "Where is Shaorong?
translations.idiomatic: As the wine flowed and music began, the Zhuangzong recounted his battles through the years, then glanced about and asked, "Where is Shaorong?

sentences.zh: 」所司奏云：「有敕，使相預會，紹榮散官，殿上無位。

translations.literal: " The responsible office reported: "By imperial order, when chief commissioners attend, Shaorong holds a scattered office and has no seat in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: " The master of ceremonies replied, "By imperial order, when chief commissioners attend, Shaorong holds only a nominal rank and has no place in the hall.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗徹會不懌。

translations.literal: " The Zhuangzong dismissed the banquet displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhuangzong broke up the banquet in displeasure.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以行欽為同平章事，由是不宴百官於內殿，但宴武臣而已，

translations.literal: The next day he made Xingqin a co-equal chief councilor; from then on he no longer banqueted the civil officials in the inner hall, but banqueted only military officers,
translations.idiomatic: The next day he appointed Xingqin co-equal chief councilor. Thereafter he no longer entertained the civil officials in the inner hall, but held banquets only for military men,

sentences.zh: 三年，行欽喪婦。

translations.literal: In the third year, Xingqin lost his wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign, Xingqin lost his wife.

sentences.zh: 莊宗有所愛宮人生皇子者，劉皇后心忌之，會行欽入侍，莊宗勞之曰：「紹榮喪婦復娶耶！

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong had a favored palace woman who bore a prince; Empress Liu was jealous at heart. When Xingqin came in attendance, the Zhuangzong comforted him and said: "Shaorong, your wife has died—will you marry again!"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong favored a palace woman who had borne him a son, and Empress Liu resented her. When Xingqin came to attend him, the Zhuangzong said kindly, "Shaorong, now that your wife is dead, will you take another!"

sentences.zh: 吾給爾婚財。

translations.literal: I will provide your marriage gifts.
translations.idiomatic: I will supply your wedding gifts.

sentences.zh: 」皇后指所忌宮人謂莊宗曰：「皇帝憐紹榮，可使為婦。

translations.literal: " The empress pointed to the palace woman she resented and said to the Zhuangzong: "The Emperor pities Shaorong—she may be made his wife.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress pointed at the woman she envied and said to the Zhuangzong, "Your Majesty pities Shaorong—let her become his wife.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗難違所請，微許之。

translations.literal: " The Zhuangzong found it hard to refuse the request and faintly assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The Zhuangzong could hardly refuse and gave a reluctant assent.

sentences.zh: 皇后即命紹榮謝之，未退，肩輿已出。

translations.literal: The empress immediately ordered Shaorong to thank her; before he had withdrawn, a sedan chair had already been sent out.
translations.idiomatic: The empress at once ordered Shaorong to give thanks. Before he could withdraw, a sedan chair had already been dispatched.

sentences.zh: 莊宗心不懌，佯不豫者累日，業已遣去，無如之何。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong was displeased at heart; he feigned illness for several days. The woman had already been sent away, and there was nothing he could do.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong was inwardly displeased and feigned illness for days, but the woman had already been sent off and nothing could be undone.

sentences.zh: 及貝州軍亂，趙在禮入魏州，莊宗方擇將，皇后曰：「小事不勞大將，促紹榮指揮可也。

translations.literal: When the Beizhou army mutinied and Zhao Zaili entered Weizhou, the Zhuangzong was just selecting a general; the empress said: "A small matter need not trouble a great general—hurry Shaorong to command and that will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Beizhou garrison mutinied and Zhao Zaili seized Weizhou, the Zhuangzong was choosing a commander. The empress said, "A trifling affair need not tie up a great general—send Shaorong to take command at once.

sentences.zh: 」乃以行欽為鄴都行營招撫使，領騎二千進討。

translations.literal: " He thereupon made Xingqin commissioner for pacification of the Ye capital field headquarters, leading two thousand cavalry to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingqin was appointed commissioner for pacification of the Ye capital field headquarters and led two thousand cavalry against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 洎至鄴城，攻之不能下，退保於澶州。

translations.literal: When he reached Ye city, he attacked but could not take it, and withdrew to hold Chuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Ye, he besieged the city but could not capture it and fell back to hold Chuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸道之師稍集，復進軍於鄴城之南。

translations.literal: Before long the armies of the various circuits gradually assembled, and he again advanced his army south of Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long troops from the various circuits gathered, and he advanced again to the south of Ye.

sentences.zh: 及明宗為帥，領軍至鄴，行欽來謁於軍中，拜起之際，誤呼萬歲者再，明宗驚駭，遏之方止。

translations.literal: When the Mingzong became commander-in-chief and led the army to Ye, Xingqin came to pay his respects in the camp; as he rose from bowing he twice mistakenly cried "Long live!" The Mingzong was startled and alarmed, and only when restrained did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mingzong took command and marched to Ye, Xingqin came to pay his respects in camp. As he rose from his bow he twice cried "Long live the Emperor!" by mistake. The Mingzong was shocked and had to silence him before he stopped.

sentences.zh: 既而明宗營於城西，行欽營於城南。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the Mingzong encamped west of the city and Xingqin encamped south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingzong then encamped west of the city and Xingqin south of it.

sentences.zh: 三月八日夜，明宗為亂軍所迫，惟行欽之軍不動，按甲以自固。

translations.literal: On the night of the eighth day of the third month, the Mingzong was pressed by the mutinous army; only Xingqin's army did not move, holding their armor to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the eighth day of the third month the Mingzong was driven by the mutineers, but only Xingqin's troops held their ground, keeping their armor on and standing firm.

sentences.zh: 明宗密令張虔釗至行欽營，戒之曰：「且堅壁勿動，計會同殺亂軍，莫錯疑誤。

translations.literal: The Mingzong secretly ordered Zhang Qianzhao to go to Xingqin's camp and warn him: "For now hold the walls and do not move; we plan to join in killing the mutinous army together—do not mistake and err.
translations.idiomatic: The Mingzong secretly sent Zhang Qianzhao to Xingqin's camp with this warning: "Hold your position and do not move. We mean to join forces and destroy the mutineers—do not misread the situation.

sentences.zh: 」行欽不聽，將步騎萬人棄甲而退。

translations.literal: " Xingqin would not listen; he led ten thousand infantry and cavalry, cast off their armor, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingqin refused to listen. He led ten thousand foot and horse, threw off their armor, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 自知失策，且保衛州，因誣奏明宗曰：「鎮師已入賊軍，終不為國使。

translations.literal: Knowing he had blundered, he meanwhile held Weizhou and thereupon falsely memorialized against the Mingzong: "The commander of the circuit army has already entered the rebel army and will never serve the state again.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing his mistake, he fell back to hold Weizhou and sent a false report accusing the Mingzong: "The circuit commander has gone over to the rebels and will never again serve the throne.

sentences.zh: 」明宗既劫出鄴城，令人走馬上章，申理其事，言：「臣且於近郡聽進止。

translations.literal: " After the Mingzong had been carried out of Ye city by force, he sent a man on a galloping horse to submit a memorial clarifying the matter, saying: "Your servant will for the present await orders in a nearby prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " After the Mingzong had been seized and carried out of Ye, he sent a rider with a memorial explaining the affair: "Your servant will await further orders in a nearby prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗覽奏釋然曰：「吾知紹榮妄矣。

translations.literal: " When the Zhuangzong read the memorial he said with relief: "I know Shaorong has lied.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Zhuangzong read the memorial he said with relief, "I knew Shaorong's report was false.

sentences.zh: 」因令白從訓與明宗子繼璟至軍前，欲令見明宗，行欽縶繼璟於路。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Bai Congxun and the Mingzong's son Jijing to go to the front of the army, intending to have them see the Mingzong; Xingqin bound Jijing on the road.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Bai Congxun and the Mingzong's son Jijing to the front, intending that they should see the Mingzong, but Xingqin seized Jijing on the way.

sentences.zh: 明宗凡奏軍機，拘留不達，故旬日之間，音驛斷絕。

translations.literal: Whenever the Mingzong memorialized on military affairs, they were detained and not delivered; therefore within ten days communications by courier were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Every memorial the Mingzong sent on military affairs was intercepted, and for ten days no word reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗出成皋，知明宗在黎陽，復令繼璟渡河召明宗，行欽即殺之，仍勸班師。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangzong marched out of Chenggao and learned the Mingzong was at Liyang, he again ordered Jijing to cross the river and summon the Mingzong; Xingqin immediately killed him and still urged withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuangzong marched out of Chenggao and learned the Mingzong was at Liyang, he again ordered Jijing to cross the river and summon him. Xingqin killed Jijing at once and pressed for a general withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 四月一日，莊宗既崩，行欽引皇后、存渥，得七百騎出師子門，將之河中就存霸，沿路部下解散，從者數騎而已。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, after the Zhuangzong had died, Xingqin led the empress and Cunwo, mustering seven hundred horsemen to go out the Shizi Gate, intending to go to Hezhong to join Cunba; along the road his subordinates dispersed, and only a few horsemen followed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month, after the Zhuangzong's death, Xingqin escorted the empress and Cunwo with seven hundred horsemen out the Shizi Gate, intending to flee to Hezhong and join Cunba. Along the way his men deserted until only a handful of riders remained.

sentences.zh: 四日，至平陸縣界，為百姓所擒，縣令裴進折其足，檻車以獻。

translations.literal: On the fourth day he reached the border of Pinglu County and was seized by the common people; the magistrate Pei Jin broke his legs and sent him in a caged cart as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day he reached Pinglu County, where the local people seized him. Magistrate Pei Jin broke his legs and sent him to the capital in a cage cart.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，詔削奪行欽在位官爵，斬於洛陽。

translations.literal: When the Mingzong took the throne, an edict stripped Xingqin of his offices and titles while in post, and he was executed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Mingzong took the throne, an edict stripped Xingqin of all his offices and titles, and he was executed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 夏魯奇，字邦傑，青州人也。

translations.literal: Xia Luqi, courtesy name Bangjie, was a man of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Luqi, whose courtesy name was Bangjie, was a native of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 初事宣武軍為軍校，與主將不協，遂歸於莊宗，以為護衛指揮使。

translations.literal: He first served the Xuanwu army as a military officer; he did not get along with the chief commander, and therefore went over to the Zhuangzong, who made him commander of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the Xuanwu army as a junior officer. At odds with his commander, he defected to the Zhuangzong, who appointed him commander of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 從周德威攻幽州，燕將有單廷珪、元行欽，時稱驍勇，魯奇與之鬥，兩不能解，將士皆釋兵縱觀。

translations.literal: Following Zhou Dewei in the attack on Youzhou, among the Yan generals were Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin, then famed for fierce bravery; Luqi fought them, and neither could break off; officers and soldiers all laid down their weapons and watched freely.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning with Zhou Dewei against Youzhou, he fought the Yan generals Shan Tinggui and Yuan Xingqin, both renowned for valor. Luqi grappled with them until neither side could break away, while soldiers on both sides laid down their arms to watch.

sentences.zh: 幽州平，魯奇功居多。

translations.literal: When Youzhou was pacified, Luqi's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou fell, Luqi's contribution was the greatest of all.

sentences.zh: 梁將劉鄩在洹水，莊宗深入致師，鄩設伏於魏縣西南葭蘆中。

translations.literal: The Liang general Liu Yan was at the Huan River; the Zhuangzong advanced deep to offer battle, and Yan set an ambush in the reed marshes southwest of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Liu Yan held the Huan River. The Zhuangzong advanced deep into enemy territory to provoke battle, and Yan laid an ambush in the reed marshes southwest of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 莊宗不滿千騎，汴人伏兵萬餘，大噪而起，圍莊宗數重。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand horsemen; the Bian men had more than ten thousand in ambush; they rose with a great clamor and surrounded the Zhuangzong in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong had fewer than a thousand riders when more than ten thousand Bian troops sprang from ambush with a great shout and surrounded him in layer after layer.

sentences.zh: 魯奇與王門關、烏德兒等奮命決戰，自午至申，俄而李存審兵至方解。

translations.literal: Luqi with Wang Menguan, Wu De'er, and others fought desperately; from the hour wu to the hour shen, and shortly Li Cunshen's troops arrived and only then was the siege broken.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi, Wang Menguan, Wu De'er, and others fought for their lives from noon until mid-afternoon before Li Cunshen's reinforcements arrived and broke the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 魯奇持槍攜劍，獨衛莊宗，手殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Luqi bore spear and carried sword, alone guarding the Zhuangzong, and with his own hand killed more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi fought with spear in one hand and sword in the other, shielding the Zhuangzong alone and killing more than a hundred men with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 烏德兒等被擒，魯奇傷痍遍體，自是莊宗尤憐之，曆磁州刺史。

translations.literal: Wu De'er and others were captured; Luqi's wounds covered his whole body; from then on the Zhuangzong especially favored him, and he served as prefect of Ci Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu De'er and others were taken prisoner. Luqi was covered with wounds, and from then on the Zhuangzong favored him all the more. He later served as prefect of Ci Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中都之戰，汴人大敗，魯奇見王彥章，識之，單馬追及，槍擬其頸；

translations.literal: In the battle of Zhongdu the Bian men were greatly defeated; Luqi saw Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, pursued on a single horse and caught up, and pressed his spear to Yanzhang's neck;
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Zhongdu the Bian army was routed. Luqi spotted Wang Yanzhang, recognized him, chased him down alone, and pressed his spear to Yanzhang's neck;

sentences.zh: 彥章顧曰：「爾非餘故人乎？

translations.literal: Yanzhang looked back and said: "Are you not an old acquaintance of mine?
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhang looked back and said, "Aren't you an old friend of mine?

sentences.zh: 」即擒之以獻。

translations.literal: " He thereupon seized him and presented him as captive.
translations.idiomatic: " He then seized him and presented him as a captive.

sentences.zh: 莊宗壯之，賞絹千匹。

translations.literal: The Zhuangzong admired his feat and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuangzong was impressed and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·趙庭隱傳》：王彥章守中都，庭隱在其軍中。

translations.literal: (From the 《Jiuguozhi · Biography of Zhao Tingyin》: Wang Yanzhang defended Zhongdu, and Tingyin was in his army.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Records of the Nine States · Biography of Zhao Tingyin》: Wang Yanzhang held Zhongdu, and Tingyin served in his army.

sentences.zh: 及彥章敗，庭隱為莊宗所獲，將以就戮，大將夏魯奇奏曰：「此矬也，其材可用。

translations.literal: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was captured by the Zhuangzong and was about to be put to death; the great general Xia Luqi memorialized: "This is a dwarf, but his talent can be used.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhang was defeated, Tingyin was captured by the Zhuangzong and was to be executed. The great general Xia Luqi memorialized, "He is a dwarf, but his abilities are useful.

sentences.zh: 」遂釋之。）〉

translations.literal: " He was thereupon released.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " He was then released.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁平，授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: When the Liang was pacified, he was appointed defender of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang was conquered, he was appointed defender of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，授河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 天成初，移鎮許州，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was transferred to garrison Xuzhou and given the additional title of co-equal chief councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he was transferred to Xuzhou as military governor and made co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 魯奇性忠義，尤通吏道，撫民有術。

translations.literal: Luqi's nature was loyal and righteous; he was especially versed in the ways of officials and had skill in comforting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi was loyal and upright by nature, especially skilled in administration, and knew how to govern the people well.

sentences.zh: 及移鎮許田，孟州之民，萬眾遮道，斷鐙臥轍，五日不發。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to garrison Xutian, the people of Meng Prefecture, tens of thousands strong, blocked the road, broke the stirrups and lay across the wheel ruts, and for five days he could not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When he was transferred to Xutian, tens of thousands of people from Meng Prefecture blocked his path, broke his stirrups, and lay across his carriage wheels so that for five days he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 父老詣闕請留，明宗令中使諭之，方得離州。

translations.literal: The elders went to the court to request that he stay; the Mingzong ordered a palace envoy to explain to them, and only then was he able to leave the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The elders petitioned the court to keep him. The Mingzong sent a palace envoy to reason with them, and only then could Luqi leave the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明宗討荊南，魯奇為副招討使，頃之，移鎮遂州。

translations.literal: When the Mingzong campaigned against Jingnan, Luqi served as deputy commissioner for pacification; shortly afterward he was transferred to garrison Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mingzong campaigned against Jingnan, Luqi served as deputy pacification commissioner. Soon afterward he was transferred to Suizhou.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李仁罕傳》：夏魯奇稟朝廷之命，繕治甲兵，將圖蜀，孟知祥與董璋謀先取魯奇，令仁罕攻遂州。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Jiuguozhi · Biography of Li Renhan》: Xia Luqi received the court's orders, repaired armor and weapons, and was about to scheme against Shu; Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted to take Luqi first and ordered Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Records of the Nine States · Biography of Li Renhan》: Xia Luqi, acting on court orders, repaired armor and weapons and prepared to move against Shu. Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang plotted to strike Luqi first and sent Renhan to attack Suizhou.)〉

sentences.zh: 董璋之叛，與孟知祥攻遂州，援路斷絕，兵盡食窮，

translations.literal: When Dong Zhang rebelled, he joined Meng Zhixiang in attacking Suizhou; the relief routes were cut off, the troops exhausted and food spent,
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhang rebelled, he and Meng Zhixiang attacked Suizhou. Relief routes were cut, supplies ran out, and the garrison was starving,

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·李肇傳》：蜀師圍夏魯奇於遂州，唐師來援，劍門不守，肇領兵赴普安以拒之，唐師不得進。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Jiuguozhi · Biography of Li Zhao》: The Shu army besieged Xia Luqi at Suizhou; Tang troops came to relieve him; Jianmen was not held; Zhao led troops to Pu'an to resist them, and the Tang army could not advance.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Records of the Nine States · Biography of Li Zhao》: Shu forces besieged Xia Luqi at Suizhou. When Tang relief troops came, Jianmen had fallen, and Zhao led troops to Pu'an to block them so that the Tang army could not advance.)〉

sentences.zh: 魯奇自刎而卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Luqi cut his own throat and died; he was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi took his own life by cutting his throat. He was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝聞其死也，慟哭之，厚給其家，贈太師、齊國公。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of his death, he wept bitterly for him, gave his family generous provision, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of his death, he wept bitterly, gave his family generous support, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 姚洪，本梁之小校也。

translations.literal: Yao Hong was originally a junior officer of the Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong had originally been a junior officer in the Liang army.

sentences.zh: 在梁時，經事董璋，長興初，率兵千人戍閬州。

translations.literal: While in the Liang he had once served Dong Zhang; at the beginning of Changxing he led a thousand troops to garrison Lang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang service he had once served under Dong Zhang. At the beginning of the Changxing era he led a thousand men to garrison Lang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 璋叛，領眾攻閬州，璋密令人誘洪，洪以大義拒之。

translations.literal: When Zhang rebelled, he led his forces to attack Lang Prefecture; Zhang secretly sent someone to entice Hong, and Hong refused on grounds of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang rebelled, he marched on Lang Prefecture and secretly sent envoys to win Hong over, but Hong refused on grounds of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及璋攻城，洪悉力拒守者三日，禦備既竭，城陷被擒。

translations.literal: When Zhang attacked the city, Hong defended with all his strength for three days; defenses were exhausted, the city fell, and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang besieged the city, Hong defended with all his strength for three days until supplies were exhausted, the city fell, and he was taken.

sentences.zh: 璋謂洪曰：「爾頃為健兒，由吾獎拔至此；

translations.literal: Zhang said to Hong: "You were once a stalwart fighter whom I promoted and raised to this position;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said to Hong, "You were once a common soldier whom I raised to your present rank;

sentences.zh: 吾書誘諭，投之於側，何相負耶？

translations.literal: I wrote letters to entice and instruct you and cast them aside—why have you betrayed me?
translations.idiomatic: I sent you letters urging you to join me. Why have you betrayed me?

sentences.zh: 」洪大罵曰：「老賊，爾為天子鎮帥，何苦反耶！

translations.literal: " Hong cursed loudly: "Old bandit, you are a frontier commander appointed by the Son of Heaven—why must you rebel!
translations.idiomatic: " Hong shouted back, "You old traitor! You were a frontier commander appointed by the Son of Heaven—why turn rebel!

sentences.zh: 爾既辜恩背主，吾與爾何恩，而雲相負！

translations.literal: You have already failed in grace and betrayed your lord—what grace is there between you and me, that you speak of betrayal!
translations.idiomatic: You have betrayed your sovereign—what debt do I owe you that you speak of betrayal!

sentences.zh: 爾為李七郎奴，掃馬糞，得一臠殘炙，感恩無盡。

translations.literal: You were a slave of Li the Seventh, sweeping horse dung; you received a scrap of leftover roast and felt endless gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: You were once Li the Seventh's servant, mucking out stables, and you were endlessly grateful for a scrap of leftover meat.

sentences.zh: 今明天子付與茅土，貴為諸侯，而驅徒結黨，圖為反噬。

translations.literal: Now the enlightened Son of Heaven has granted you a fief and ennobled you as a feudal lord, yet you drive your followers and form factions, plotting to turn and bite back.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Son of Heaven has granted you a fief and made you a feudal lord, yet you rally followers and plot rebellion against your benefactor.

sentences.zh: 爾本奴才，則無恥；

translations.literal: You were born a slave, so you have no shame;
translations.idiomatic: You were born a slave, so you have no shame.

sentences.zh: 吾忠義之士，不忍為也。

translations.literal: I am a man of loyalty and righteousness—I cannot bear to do such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of loyalty and righteousness and cannot stoop to that.

sentences.zh: 吾可為天子死，不能與人奴苟生！

translations.literal: I can die for the Son of Heaven, but I cannot live on in shame as another man's slave!
translations.idiomatic: I can die for the Son of Heaven, but I will not live on as another man's lackey!

sentences.zh: 」璋怒，令軍士十人，持刀刲割其膚，燃鑊於前，自取啖食，洪至死大罵不已。

translations.literal: " Zhang was enraged and ordered ten soldiers with knives to slice his flesh; a cauldron was heated before him, and Zhang himself took the flesh and ate it; Hong cursed without cease until death.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang in fury ordered ten soldiers to carve slices from Hong's flesh, heated a cauldron before him, and ate the flesh himself. Hong cursed him without cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 明宗聞之泣下，置洪二子於近衛，給賜甚厚。

translations.literal: When the Mingzong heard of it he wept; he placed Hong's two sons in the inner guard and gave them very generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mingzong heard of it he wept, enrolled Hong's two sons in the inner guard, and gave them generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 李嚴，幽州人，本名讓坤。

translations.literal: Li Yan, a man of Youzhou, original name Rangkun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, a native of Youzhou, was originally named Rangkun.

sentences.zh: 初仕燕，為刺史，涉獵書傳，便弓馬，有口辯，多遊藝，以功名自許。

translations.literal: He first served Yan as a prefectural governor, ranged widely in books and records, was skilled in bow and horse, had eloquence, and was accomplished in many arts; he aspired to merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Yan as a prefect, read widely in the classics, was skilled in archery and horsemanship, eloquent in speech, and accomplished in many arts, and he aspired to merit and fame.

sentences.zh: 同光中，為客省使。

translations.literal: During Tongguang he served as commissioner of the reception office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era he served as commissioner of the reception office.

sentences.zh: 奉使於蜀，及與王衍相見，陳使者之禮，因於笏記中具述莊宗興復之功，其警句云：「才過汶水，縛王彥章於馬前；

translations.literal: On a mission to Shu, when he met Wang Yan, he set forth the protocol of an envoy and, in notes on his tablet, fully recounted the Zhuangzong's achievements in restoration; a striking line read: "Having just crossed the Wen River, he bound Wang Yanzhang before his horse;
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Shu, when he met Wang Yan he observed the protocol of an envoy and, in notes on his tablet, recounted the Zhuangzong's restoration of the Tang. A striking passage ran: "Hardly past the Wen River, he bound Wang Yanzhang before his horse;

sentences.zh: 旋及夷門，斬朱友貞於樓上。

translations.literal: then reaching Yimen, he beheaded Zhu Youzhen on the tower.
translations.idiomatic: then at Yimen he beheaded Zhu Youzhen on the tower."

sentences.zh: 」嚴復聲韻清亮，蜀人聽之愕然。

translations.literal: " Yan recited it again with clear, resonant tones; the Shu people who heard it were startled.
translations.idiomatic: Yan recited it again in a clear, resonant voice, and the Shu listeners were stunned.

sentences.zh: 時蜀偽樞密使宋光嗣召嚴曲宴，因以近事訊於嚴。

translations.literal: At that time the Shu pretender's commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Song Guangsi summoned Yan to a private banquet and thereupon questioned him about recent events.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu pretender's commissioner of military affairs Song Guangsi then invited Yan to a private banquet and questioned him about recent events.

sentences.zh: 嚴對曰：「吾皇前年四月即位於鄴宮，當月下鄆州。

translations.literal: Yan replied: "Our emperor in the fourth month two years ago took the throne at the Ye palace; that same month he descended on Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied, "Our emperor took the throne at Ye in the fourth month two years ago and that same month marched on Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十月四日，親統萬騎破賊中都，乘勝鼓行，遂誅汴孽，偽梁尚有兵三十萬，謀臣猛將，解甲倒戈。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally commanded ten thousand horsemen and broke the rebels at Zhongdu; riding the victory he beat the drums and advanced, and thereupon executed the Bian usurpers; the false Liang still had three hundred thousand troops, strategists and fierce generals, who doffed armor and turned their weapons.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the tenth month he personally led ten thousand horsemen and crushed the rebels at Zhongdu. Pressing the victory, he marched on and destroyed the Bian regime. Though the false Liang still had three hundred thousand troops, their strategists and fierce generals laid down arms and turned their coats.

sentences.zh: 西盡甘、涼，東漸海外，南逾閩、浙，北極幽陵。

translations.literal: West to the limit of Gan and Liang, east gradually to beyond the sea, south beyond Min and Zhe, north to the utmost of Youling.
translations.idiomatic: His realm reached west to Gan and Liang, east to the sea, south beyond Min and Zhe, and north to Youling.

sentences.zh: 牧伯侯王，稱藩不暇，家財入貢，府實上供。

translations.literal: Pastoral lords and feudal kings had no leisure to declare themselves vassals; family wealth entered as tribute, and treasury stores were sent up as supply.
translations.idiomatic: Regional lords and feudal kings vied to declare themselves vassals; they sent family wealth as tribute and filled the imperial storehouses with supplies.

sentences.zh: 吳國本朝舊臣，岐下先皇元老，遣子入侍，述職稱藩。

translations.literal: Wu was an old subject of our dynasty; the elder statesman below Qi sent his son to attend court and reported his duties as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, a former subject of our court, and the veteran minister below Qi sent their sons to serve at court and paid homage as vassals.

sentences.zh: 淮、海之君，卑辭厚貢，湖湘、荊楚，杭越、甌閩，異貨奇珍，府無虛月。

translations.literal: The lords of Huai and the sea used humble words and heavy tribute; from Huguang, Jingchu, Hang-Yue, and Ou-Min came exotic goods and rare treasures, and the treasury had no empty month.
translations.idiomatic: Lords along the Huai and the coast sent humble embassies with rich tribute. From Huguang, Jingchu, Hangzhou, Yue, and the Min coast came exotic goods and curios so that the imperial storehouses were never empty for a month.

sentences.zh: 吾皇以德懷來，以威款附。

translations.literal: Our emperor by virtue draws men in, and by might wins their attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor wins men by virtue and binds them by might.

sentences.zh: 順則涵之以恩澤，逆則問之以干戈，四海車書，大同非晚。

translations.literal: Those who submit he bathes in grace; those who resist he confronts with arms; the four seas with chariots and writing—great unity is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submit he showers with grace; those who resist he meets with arms. When chariots and writing unite the four seas, universal peace will not be long delayed.

sentences.zh: 」光嗣曰：「餘所未知，惟岐下宋公，我之姻好，洞見其心，反覆多端，專謀跋扈，大不足信也。

translations.literal: " Guangsi said: "Of the rest I do not know; only Lord Song below Qi, my kinsman by marriage—I see through his heart: he is changeable in many ways and plots arrogance alone; he is greatly untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangsi said, "Of the rest I cannot speak, but Lord Song below Qi is my kinsman by marriage and I know his heart well. He is treacherous and schemes only for his own power—he is utterly untrustworthy.

sentences.zh: 似聞契丹部族，近日稍強，大國可無慮乎？

translations.literal: I seem to hear that the Khitan tribes have grown somewhat stronger of late—can the great state be without concern?
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Khitan tribes have grown stronger lately. Surely your great state has no worries on that account?

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「子言契丹之強盛，孰若偽梁？

translations.literal: " Yan said: "You speak of the Khitan's strength—how does it compare with the false Liang?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "You speak of Khitan strength—how does it compare with the false Liang?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「比梁差劣也。

translations.literal: " He said: "Compared with the Liang, they are rather inferior.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "They are rather weaker than the Liang.

sentences.zh: 」嚴曰：「吾國視契丹如蚤虱耳，以其無害，不足爬搔。

translations.literal: " Yan said: "Our state regards the Khitan as fleas and lice, because they do no harm and are not worth scratching.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan said, "Our state regards the Khitan as fleas and lice—harmless vermin not worth troubling over.

sentences.zh: 吾良將勁兵布天下，彼不勞一郡之兵，一校之眾，則懸首槀街，盡為奴擄。

translations.literal: Our good generals and strong troops are spread across the realm; they would need neither the troops of one commandery nor the men of one colonel—heads would hang on the gallows street and all would become slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Our finest generals and strongest troops are posted across the realm. We would not need even one commandery's army or one colonel's men to hang their heads on the execution ground and make slaves of them all.

sentences.zh: 但以天生四夷，當置度外，不在九州之本，未欲窮兵黷武也。

translations.literal: But because the four barbarians are born of Heaven, they should be set beyond measure, not within the root of the Nine Provinces; we do not yet wish to exhaust the army in reckless warfare.
translations.idiomatic: But the four barbarians are Heaven's creation and lie outside our core realm. We have no wish to exhaust the army in reckless war.

sentences.zh: 」光嗣聞辯對，畏而奇之。

translations.literal: " When Guangsi heard this eloquent reply, he feared him and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangsi, hearing this reply, was both intimidated and impressed.

sentences.zh: 時王衍失政，嚴知其可取，使還具奏，故平蜀之謀，始於嚴。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yan's government was failing; Yan knew he could be taken and, on returning, submitted a full memorial; thus the plan to pacify Shu began with Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan's rule was failing, and Yan saw that Shu could be taken. On his return he memorialized in full, and the plan to conquer Shu began with him.

sentences.zh: 郭崇韜起軍之日，以嚴為三川招撫使，嚴與先鋒使康延孝將兵五千，先驅閣道，或馳以詞說，或威以兵鋒，大軍未及，所在降下。

translations.literal: On the day Guo Chongtao raised the army, he made Yan commissioner for pacification of the Three Rivers; Yan with the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led five thousand troops, advancing first along the plank roads, sometimes galloping to persuade with words, sometimes awing with the edge of arms; before the main army arrived, places everywhere submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Chongtao marched, he appointed Yan commissioner for pacification of the Three Rivers. Yan and the vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led five thousand men ahead along the plank roads, sometimes winning surrender by persuasion, sometimes by the threat of arms. Before the main army arrived, city after city submitted.

sentences.zh: 延孝在漢州，王衍與書曰：「 可請李司空先來，餘即舉城納款。

translations.literal: Yanxiao was at Han Prefecture; Wang Yan wrote to him: "You may ask Minister Li to come first; I will then surrender the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxiao was at Han Prefecture when Wang Yan wrote to him: "Ask Minister Li to come first, and I will surrender the whole city.

sentences.zh: 」眾咸以討蜀之謀始於嚴，衍以甘言，將誘而殺之，欲不令往。

translations.literal: " All agreed that the plan to attack Shu had begun with Yan; Yan intended with sweet words to lure and kill him, and wished not to let him go.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone said the Shu campaign had been Yan's idea and that Wang Yan's kind words were a trap to lure and kill him, and they tried to keep Yan from going.

sentences.zh: 嚴聞之喜，即馳騎入益州，衍見嚴於母前，以母、妻為托。

translations.literal: Yan heard this with joy and immediately galloped into Yizhou; Yan met Yan before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was delighted and rode at once into Yizhou. Wang Yan received him before his mother and entrusted his mother and wife to Yan's care.

sentences.zh: 即日，引蜀使歐陽彬迎謁魏王繼岌。

translations.literal: That same day he led the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to welcome and pay respects to Prince of Wei Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he brought the Shu envoy Ouyang Bin to pay respects to Prince of Wei Jiji.

sentences.zh: 蜀平班師，會明宗即位，遷泗州防禦使兼客省使。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified the army returned; coinciding with the Mingzong's accession, he was transferred to defender of Si Prefecture while also serving as commissioner of the reception office.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified the army withdrew. When the Mingzong took the throne, Yan was made defender of Si Prefecture and commissioner of the reception office.

sentences.zh: 長興初，安重誨謀欲控製兩川，嚴乃求為西川兵馬都監，庶效方略。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, An Chonghui plotted to control the Two Rivers; Yan thereupon requested to be overall military inspector of western Shu, hoping to put his strategies into effect.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changxing era An Chonghui sought to control the Two Rivers, and Yan asked to be made overall military inspector of western Shu so that he might put his plans into effect.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥覺之，既至，執而害之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang perceived this; once Yan arrived, he seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang saw through him, and when Yan arrived he seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: （《九國誌·王彥銖傳》：李嚴之為監軍也，密懷異謀，知祥數其過，命彥銖擒斬之，嚴之左右無敢動者。）〉

translations.literal: (From the 《Jiuguozhi · Biography of Wang Yanzhu》: When Li Yan served as army inspector, he secretly harbored a different design; Zhixiang counted his faults and ordered Yanzhu to seize and behead him; none of Yan's attendants dared move.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Records of the Nine States · Biography of Wang Yanzhu》: When Li Yan served as army inspector he secretly plotted treachery. Zhixiang listed his offenses and ordered Yanzhu to seize and behead him; none of Yan's attendants dared stir.)〉

sentences.zh: 贈太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 嚴之母，賢明婦人。

translations.literal: Yan's mother was a wise and discerning woman.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's mother was a wise and virtuous woman.

sentences.zh: 初，嚴將赴蜀，母曰：「汝前啟破蜀之謀，今又入蜀，將死報蜀人矣！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yan was about to go to Shu, his mother said: "You earlier opened the plan to destroy Shu; now you enter Shu again—you will die to repay the people of Shu!
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was about to go to Shu, his mother said, "You were the one who proposed destroying Shu. Now you go into Shu again—you will die at the hands of the Shu people!

sentences.zh: 與汝永訣。

translations.literal: I take eternal leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: This is our final parting.

sentences.zh: 」既而果如其言。

translations.literal: " Before long it indeed came to pass as she had said.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end it happened exactly as she had foretold.

sentences.zh: 李仁矩，本明宗在藩鎮時客將也。

translations.literal: Li Renju was originally a guest general when the Mingzong was in the frontier commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renju had originally been a guest officer when the Mingzong held a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，錄其趨走之勞，擢居內職，復為安重誨所庇，故數年之間，遷為客省使、左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Mingzong took the throne, he recorded his labors in attendance and promoted him to inner service; he was again sheltered by An Chonghui, and within several years was transferred to commissioner of the reception office and great general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mingzong took the throne he rewarded Renju's service in attendance and brought him into the inner court. Protected by An Chonghui, within a few years he rose to commissioner of the reception office and great general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 天成中，因奉使東川，董璋張筵以召之，仁矩貪於館舍，與倡妓酣飲，日既中而不至，大為璋所詬辱，自是深銜之。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng, on a mission to eastern Shu, Dong Zhang spread a banquet to summon him; Renju lingered greedily at the lodge, drinking deep with singing girls; the sun had passed midday and he did not come—Zhang greatly reviled and humiliated him, and from then on bore a deep grudge.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era, on a mission to eastern Shu, Dong Zhang held a banquet for him, but Renju lingered at his lodgings drinking with courtesans until past noon and never appeared. Zhang reviled him harshly, and from then on bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 長興初，璋既跋扈於東川，重誨奏以仁矩為閬州節度使，俾伺璋之反狀，時物議以為不可。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, Zhang was already arrogant in eastern Shu; Chonghui memorialized to make Renju military governor of Lang Prefecture, so that he might watch for signs of Zhang's rebellion; at the time public opinion held this unwise.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changxing era Zhang was already overbearing in eastern Shu. Chonghui petitioned to make Renju military governor of Lang Prefecture to watch for signs of rebellion, though public opinion held this unwise.

sentences.zh: 及仁矩至鎮，偵璋所為，曲形奏報，地裏遐僻，朝廷莫知事實，激成璋之逆節，由仁矩也。

translations.literal: When Renju reached his post, he spied on Zhang's actions and reported them in distorted form; the region was remote and secluded, and the court did not know the facts—Zhang's rebellious course was provoked by Renju.
translations.idiomatic: When Renju reached his post he spied on Zhang and sent distorted reports to the court. The region was remote and the court knew no better, and Zhang's rebellion was largely provoked by Renju.

sentences.zh: 長興元年冬十月，璋自率凶黨，以攻其城。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Changxing, Zhang personally led his vicious followers to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Changxing, Zhang personally led his followers to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 仁矩召軍校謀守戰利害，皆曰：「璋久圖反計，以賂誘士心，凶氣方盛，未可與戰，宜堅壁以守之。

translations.literal: Renju summoned military officers to discuss the advantages and disadvantages of defense and battle; all said: "Zhang has long plotted rebellion, using bribes to win soldiers' hearts; his fierce momentum is at its height—we cannot fight him yet and should hold the walls firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Renju called his officers to discuss defense. All said, "Zhang has long plotted rebellion and bought his soldiers' loyalty. His momentum is at its peak—we should not fight but hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 儻旬浹之間，大軍東至，即賊必退。

translations.literal: If within ten days the great army arrives from the east, the rebels will surely retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the main army will arrive from the east and the rebels will withdraw.

sentences.zh: 」仁矩曰：「蜀兵懦，安能當我精甲！

translations.literal: " Renju said: "Shu troops are cowardly—how can they withstand our elite armor!
translations.idiomatic: " Renju said, "Shu soldiers are cowards—how can they stand against our elite troops!

sentences.zh: 」即驅之出戰，兵未交，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: " He immediately drove them out to battle; before the armies had joined, they were defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: " He drove them out to fight at once. Before battle was joined they were routed.

sentences.zh: 既而城陷，仁矩被擒，舉族為璋所害。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the city fell; Renju was captured, and his whole clan was killed by Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the city fell. Renju was captured and Zhang killed his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 康思立，晉陽人也。

translations.literal: Kang Sili was a man of Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Sili was a native of Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，事武皇為爪牙，署河東親騎軍使。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled in mounted archery; he served the Martial Emperor as a trusted agent and was appointed commander of the Hedong personal cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he excelled at mounted archery. He served the Martial Emperor as a trusted agent and was appointed commander of the Hedong personal cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，從解圍於上黨，敗梁人於柏鄉，及平薊兵，後戰於河上，皆有功，累承製加檢校戶部尚書，右突騎指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangzong succeeded, he followed in raising the siege at Shangdang, defeated the Liang men at Baixiang, and when Ji troops were pacified, later fought on the Yellow River—all with merit; he repeatedly received edicts adding the honorary post of Minister of Revenue and commander of the Right Shock Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuangzong succeeded he fought at Shangdang, routed the Liang at Baixiang, helped pacify Ji, and later fought on the Yellow River, earning merit in each campaign. He was repeatedly promoted to honorary Minister of Revenue and commander of the Right Shock Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，繼改軍帥，賜忠勇拱衛功臣，加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangzong took the throne, he was successively made army commander, granted the title of meritorious minister of loyal valor and imperial guard, and given the additional post of honorary Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuangzong took the throne he was made army commander, granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Valor and Imperial Guard, and promoted to honorary Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 天成元年，授應州刺史，尋移嵐州，充北面諸蕃部族都監。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Ying Prefecture; shortly afterward he was moved to Lan Prefecture and served as overall inspector of the various tribal groups on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancheng he was appointed prefect of Ying Prefecture, then transferred to Lan Prefecture as overall inspector of the northern frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷宿州團練使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made regimental commissioner of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，領昭武軍節度、利巴集等州觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he took command of the Zhaowu army and served as commissioner for observation and disposition of Li, Ba, Ji, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became military governor of Zhaowu and commissioner overseeing Li, Ba, Ji, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 改賜耀忠保節功臣。

translations.literal: He was re-granted the title of meritorious minister of glorious loyalty and preservation of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the new title Meritorious Minister of Glorious Loyalty and Preservation of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 長興初，朝廷舉兵討東川董璋，詔監西面行營軍馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing the court raised troops to punish Dong Zhang of eastern Shu and ordered him to supervise the western field headquarters as overall commander of army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changxing era the court marched against Dong Zhang of eastern Shu and appointed him to supervise the western field headquarters as overall commander of army and horse.

sentences.zh: 二年，移鎮陝州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to garrison Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Shan Prefecture as military governor.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：潞王至靈寶，思立謀固守陝城以俟康義誠。

translations.literal: (From the 《Zizhi Tongjian》: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shan city firmly and await Kang Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Comprehensive Mirror》: When the Prince of Lu reached Lingbao, Sili planned to hold Shanzhou firmly and await Kang Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，捧聖五百騎戍陝，為潞王前鋒，至城下，呼城上人曰：「禁軍十萬已奉新帝，爾輩數人奚為！

translations.literal: Earlier, five hundred horsemen of the Pingsheng guard garrisoned Shan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard; reaching the foot of the wall, they called to those above: "A hundred thousand of the imperial guard have already acclaimed the new emperor—what are you few doing!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, five hundred Pingsheng cavalry garrisoned Shan as the Prince of Lu's vanguard. At the foot of the wall they shouted, "A hundred thousand imperial guards have already acclaimed the new emperor—what are you few doing here!

sentences.zh: 徒累一城人塗地耳！

translations.literal: You will only bring ruin on all the people of one city!
translations.idiomatic: You will only bring ruin on the whole city!

sentences.zh: 」於是捧聖卒爭出迎，思立不能禁，不得已，亦出迎。）〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Pingsheng soldiers vied to go out and welcome them; Sili could not restrain them and, having no choice, also went out to welcome them.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " The Pingsheng troops rushed out to welcome them. Sili could not stop them and, with no choice, went out to welcome them as well.)〉

sentences.zh: 清泰初，改授邢台，累官至檢校太傅，封會稽郡開國侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was reassigned to Xing Prefecture; he rose in office to honorary Grand Tutor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of the founding state of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was reassigned to Xing Prefecture, rose to honorary Grand Tutor, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 二年，入為右神武統軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered court as commander-in-chief of the Right Divine Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he entered court as commander-in-chief of the Right Divine Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，充北面行營馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year he served as overall commander of cavalry for the northern field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he served as overall commander of cavalry for the northern field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 是歲閏十一月，卒於軍，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year he died in the army, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eleventh month of that year he died in camp at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 張敬達，字志通，代州人，小字生鐵。

translations.literal: Zhang Jingda, courtesy name Zhitong, was a man of Dai Prefecture; his childhood name was Sheng Tie (Raw Iron).
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda, whose courtesy name was Zhitong, was a native of Daizhou; his childhood name was Raw Iron.

sentences.zh: 父審，素有勇，事武皇為列校，曆廳直軍使，同光初，卒於軍。

translations.literal: His father Shen was by nature brave; he served the Martial Emperor as a column commander, served successively as commissioner of the hall-direct guard, and in the beginning of Tongguang died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen was known for courage. He served the Martial Emperor as a column commander and later as commissioner of the hall-direct guard, and died in service early in the Tongguang era.

sentences.zh: 敬達少以騎射著名，莊宗知之，召令繼父職；

translations.literal: Jingda in youth was famed for mounted archery; the Zhuangzong knew of him and summoned him to succeed his father's post;
translations.idiomatic: Jingda was famed in youth for mounted archery. The Zhuangzong knew of him and summoned him to succeed his father's post.

sentences.zh: 平河南有功，繼加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: he had merit in pacifying Henan and was then given the additional post of honorary Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He earned merit pacifying Henan and was promoted to honorary Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，曆捧聖指揮使、檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When the Mingzong took the throne, he successively served as commander of the Pingsheng guard and honorary Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mingzong took the throne he served as commander of the Pingsheng guard and honorary Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 長興中，改河東馬步軍都指揮使，超授檢校司徒，領欽州刺史。

translations.literal: During Changxing he was made overall commander of Hedong horse and foot armies, exceptionally granted honorary Defender-in-Chief, and given charge of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era he was made overall commander of the Hedong horse and foot armies, exceptionally promoted to honorary Defender-in-Chief, and given Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，加檢校太保、應州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the additional posts of honorary Grand Guardian and military governor of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made honorary Grand Guardian and military governor of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷雲州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Yun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時以契丹率族帳自黑榆林挎剌泊至沒越泊，雲借漢界水草，敬達每聚兵塞下，以遏其衝。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan led their tribal tents from Heiyulin and Kuolapo to Meiyuepo; Yun borrowed pasture and water on Han territory, and Jingda often gathered troops below the passes to block their thrust.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then led their tribes from Heiyulin and Kuolapo to Meiyuepo, grazing their herds on Han pasture. Jingda repeatedly massed troops at the passes to block them.

sentences.zh: 契丹竟不敢南牧，邊人賴之。

translations.literal: The Khitan in the end did not dare pasture southward, and the border people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan never dared drive their herds south again, and the border people owed him their security.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，自彭門移鎮平陽，加檢校太傅，從石敬瑭為北面兵馬副總管，仍屯兵雁門。

translations.literal: During Qingtai he was moved from Pengmen to garrison Pingyang, given the additional post of honorary Grand Tutor, followed Shi Jingtang as deputy overall commander of northern army and horse, and still garrisoned troops at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era he was transferred from Pengmen to Pingyang, made honorary Grand Tutor, and served under Shi Jingtang as deputy overall commander of the northern armies while garrisoning Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，晉高祖建義，末帝詔以敬達為北面行營都招討使，仍使悉引部下兵圍太原，以定州節度使楊光遠副焉。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin Gaozu raised the righteous standard; the Last Emperor ordered Jingda as overall commissioner for pacification of the northern field headquarters, still having him lead all his subordinate troops to besiege Taiyuan, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Ding Prefecture, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Jin Gaozu rebelled. The Last Emperor appointed Jingda overall commissioner for pacification of the northern field headquarters and ordered him to besiege Taiyuan with all his troops, with Yang Guangyuan, military governor of Ding Prefecture, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 尋統兵三萬，營於晉安鄉。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he commanded thirty thousand troops and encamped at Jin'an township.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he commanded thirty thousand men and encamped at Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 末帝自六月繼有詔促令攻取，敬達設長城連柵、雲梯飛炮，使工者運其巧思，窮土木之力。

translations.literal: From the sixth month onward the Last Emperor repeatedly issued edicts urging capture; Jingda set up long walls of linked palisades, cloud ladders and flying catapults, had craftsmen apply their ingenuity, and exhausted the power of earth and wood.
translations.idiomatic: From the sixth month on the Last Emperor repeatedly ordered him to attack. Jingda built linked palisades, siege ladders, and catapults, employing every device of engineering.

sentences.zh: 時督事者每有所構，則暴風大雨，平地水深數尺，而城柵崩墮，竟不能合其圍。

translations.literal: Whenever those supervising the work made some construction, violent wind and heavy rain followed; water on level ground was several feet deep, and walls and palisades collapsed—in the end they could not close the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they built siege works, violent storms followed, flooding the plain several feet deep and collapsing walls and palisades until they could not complete the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 九月，契丹至，敬達大敗，尋為所圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived; Jingda was greatly defeated and shortly afterward was surrounded.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Khitan arrived. Jingda was routed and soon surrounded.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖及蕃眾自晉安寨南門外，長百餘里，闊五十里，布以氈帳，用毛索掛鈴，而部伍多犬，以備警急。

translations.literal: The Jin Gaozu and the barbarian hosts from outside the south gate of the Jin'an camp stretched more than a hundred li in length and fifty li in width, spread with felt tents, using wool ropes hung with bells, and the ranks had many dogs to guard against sudden alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Gaozu and the barbarian hosts spread south of the Jin'an camp for more than a hundred li in length and fifty li in width, their felt tents linked by wool ropes hung with bells, and their ranks full of dogs to give warning.

sentences.zh: 營中嘗有夜遁者，出則犬吠鈴動，跬步不能行焉。

translations.literal: When someone in the camp once fled by night, as he went out the dogs barked and the bells rang, and he could not move a single step.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone in the camp tried to flee by night, the dogs barked and the bells rang, and he could not take a single step.

sentences.zh: 自是敬達與麾下部曲五萬人，馬萬匹，無由四奔，但見穹廬如崗阜相屬，諸軍相顧失色。

translations.literal: From then on Jingda and the fifty thousand men under his command, with ten thousand horses, had no way to flee in any direction; they saw only domed tents like linked hillocks, and the armies looked at one another and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda and his fifty thousand men with ten thousand horses could flee nowhere. They saw only yurts stretching like hills, and the armies looked at one another in dismay.

sentences.zh: 始則削木篩糞，以飼其馬，日望朝廷救軍，及漸羸死，則與將士分食之，馬盡食殫。

translations.literal: At first they shaved wood and sifted dung to feed their horses, each day hoping for the court's relief army; as the horses gradually weakened and died, they shared the meat with officers and soldiers until the horses were all eaten up.
translations.idiomatic: At first they fed their horses on shaved wood and sifted dung while awaiting relief from the court. As the horses weakened and died, officers and men shared the meat until every horse was eaten.

sentences.zh: 副將楊光遠、次將安審琦知不濟，勸敬達宜早降以求自安。

translations.literal: The deputy Yang Guangyuan and the second commander An Shenqi, knowing the situation could not be saved, urged Jingda to surrender early to seek his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Yang Guangyuan and second commander An Shenqi, seeing defeat was certain, urged Jingda to surrender early to save himself.

sentences.zh: 敬達曰：「吾受恩於明宗，位曆方鎮，主上授我大柄，而失律如此，已有愧於心也。

translations.literal: Jingda said: "I received grace from the Mingzong, held posts across frontier commands, and the sovereign entrusted me with great authority—yet I have failed in discipline like this; I already have shame in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jingda said, "I owe my advancement to the Mingzong and have held frontier commands. The sovereign entrusted me with great authority, and to fail so badly already shames me.

sentences.zh: 今救軍在近，旦暮雪恥有期，諸公何相迫耶！

translations.literal: Now the relief army is near; morning and evening the day to wipe away disgrace is at hand—why do you gentlemen press me!
translations.idiomatic: Relief is near, and we may yet redeem ourselves—why do you press me so!

sentences.zh: 待勢窮，則請殺吾，攜首以降，亦未為晚。

translations.literal: When the situation is exhausted, then ask to kill me and carry my head to surrender—that would not yet be late.
translations.idiomatic: When all is lost, you may kill me and carry my head to surrender—that will be time enough.

sentences.zh: 」光遠、審琦知敬達意未決，恐坐成魚肉，遂斬敬達以降。

translations.literal: " Guangyuan and Shenqi knew Jingda's mind was not settled and feared they would sit and become fish on the chopping block; they thereupon beheaded Jingda and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangyuan and Shenqi saw that Jingda would not decide and feared they would be slaughtered like fish on a block, so they beheaded Jingda and surrendered.

sentences.zh: （《契丹國志》：楊光遠謀害張敬達，諸將高行周陰為之備，敬達疏於防禦，推遠行周等。

translations.literal: (From the 《Khitan State Annals》: Yang Guangyuan plotted to kill Zhang Jingda; the generals Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it; Jingda was lax in defense and pushed the matter onto Xingzhou and others.
translations.idiomatic: (From the 《Annals of the Khitan State》: Yang Guangyuan plotted to kill Zhang Jingda. General Gao Xingzhou secretly prepared against it, while Jingda was lax in defense and trusted Xingzhou and the others.

sentences.zh: 清晨，光遠上謁，見敬達左右無人，遂殺之。）〉

translations.literal: At early dawn Guangyuan came to pay his respects; seeing no one beside Jingda, he killed him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Guangyuan came to pay his respects. Finding no one beside Jingda, he killed him.)〉
